metadata.title: The Amazing Machine: My Body
metadata.subtitle: Discovering how our body works inside and out!
metadata.subject: EVS
metadata.author: EduOS Chief Academic Architect
learning_outcomes: Identify external body parts and their functions.
Understand the basic function of internal organs like the Brain and Heart.
Describe the 5 sense organs and how they help us explore the world.
Learn daily habits to keep the body clean and healthy.

ai_context.learning_goal: Give students a comprehensive, textbook-level understanding of the human body.
common_misconceptions: Students often think the stomach is just the belly button area.
They forget skin is a sense organ.
ai_context.tutor_hint: If a student struggles with internal organs, use the 'car engine' analogy.

blocks.title: The Ultimate Machine
blocks.body: Look at a car. A car needs wheels to move, an engine to run, and headlights to see in the dark. But did you know that YOU are a machine too? In fact, you are the most amazing, magical machine in the whole world!

blocks.question: What is the most amazing machine in the world?
blocks.explanation: Your body can heal itself, grow, run, jump, and think. No car or computer can do that!

blocks.title: Parts We Can See
blocks.body: Our body has many parts that we can see from the outside. These are called **External Organs**. Let's start from the top! First, we have the Head. Our head rests on our Neck. The neck allows us to turn our head left, right, up, and down so we can look around without moving our whole body.

blocks.front: What joins the Head to the rest of the body?

blocks.title: Arms and Legs
blocks.body: We have two arms and two legs. Together, these are called our **Limbs**. Our arms have elbows, wrists, hands, and fingers. They help us write, draw, hold a glass of water, and hug our parents! Our legs have knees, ankles, feet, and toes. They carry our weight and help us walk, run, jump, and dance.

blocks.question: Which body part helps you write in your notebook?
blocks.explanation: Our hands and fingers allow us to hold pencils and write!

blocks.title: Try this!
blocks.body: Try to pick up a pencil without bending your fingers. Can you do it? Our joints (like elbows and knuckles) make movement possible!

blocks.title: The Hidden Engine
blocks.body: We talked about parts we can see. But what is happening INSIDE your body? Just like you can't see the engine inside a car, you can't see the organs inside your body. Let's look inside!

blocks.title: The Boss: The Brain
blocks.body: Inside your head, safe inside a hard bone called the skull, sits your [DICT_C1_BRAIN|Brain]. The brain is the boss of your body. It is like a supercomputer. When you want to raise your hand, your brain sends a super-fast message to your arm telling it to move. It also helps you think, learn, and dream!

blocks.front: Which organ is the 'Boss' of the body?

blocks.title: The Pump: The Heart
blocks.body: Put your hand on the left side of your chest. Do you feel a 'thump-thump'? That is your [DICT_C1_HEART|Heart]! The heart is a very strong muscle. Its job is to pump red blood to every single part of your body. The blood carries food and oxygen to keep you alive.

blocks.title: Heartbeat Challenge
blocks.body: Jump up and down 10 times really fast! Now feel your chest again. Is your heart beating faster? It has to pump faster to give your legs energy to jump!

blocks.title: The Balloons: The Lungs
blocks.body: Take a deep breath in. Feel your chest get bigger? That is because of your [DICT_C1_LUNGS|Lungs]. You have two lungs inside your chest. They work like balloons. When you breathe in, they fill up with fresh air (Oxygen). When you breathe out, they push out the bad air.

blocks.question: Which organ works like a balloon to help us breathe?
blocks.explanation: The lungs fill with air when you take a deep breath!

blocks.title: Exploring the World
blocks.body: How do you know that a rose smells nice, or that a lemon is sour? Your brain needs spies to tell it what is happening outside! These spies are called the [DICT_C1_SENSE_ORGANS|Sense Organs].

blocks.title: 1. Eyes to See
blocks.body: Our eyes help us see the beautiful world. We can see colors like red, blue, and green. We can see if an object is far away or very close. When you watch a cartoon, you are using your eyes!

blocks.title: 2. Ears to Hear
blocks.body: Our ears help us hear sounds. We can hear the sweet chirping of birds, the loud honking of cars, and the voice of our mother calling us for dinner.

blocks.title: 3. Nose to Smell
blocks.body: Our nose helps us smell things. We can smell delicious pizza baking in the oven. But warning! It also lets us smell stinky garbage, which tells us to stay away!

blocks.title: 4. Tongue to Taste
blocks.body: Our tongue helps us taste our food. The tongue has tiny bumps on it that can tell if food is sweet (like chocolate), salty (like chips), sour (like lemon), or bitter (like medicine).

blocks.title: 5. Skin to Feel
blocks.body: Our skin covers our entire body. It is the largest sense organ! It helps us feel if something is hot, cold, soft, or rough. When you pet a fluffy cat, your skin tells your brain that it feels soft.

blocks.question: If you are eating ice cream, which sense organ tells you that it is cold?
blocks.explanation: The tongue tells you it is sweet, but the SKIN (inside your mouth and lips) feels that it is cold!

blocks.title: Don't Forget!
blocks.body: Many students think we only have skin on our hands. But skin covers our whole body! You can feel cold wind on your face or legs too.

blocks.title: Taking Care of the Machine
blocks.body: Because your body is such an amazing machine, you have to take good care of it! You should eat healthy food (like fruits and vegetables) to give it energy. You should also drink lots of water.

blocks.title: Rest and Cleanliness
blocks.body: Your brain and muscles get tired after playing all day. That is why you need 8 to 10 hours of sleep every night. We also need to keep our body clean by brushing our teeth twice a day and taking a bath. This washes away bad germs that can make us sick.

blocks.front: How many hours of sleep do you need?

blocks.title: Think about it!
blocks.body: Imagine if you had no bones in your body. What would happen? You would be like a jellyfish, completely floppy! Our skeleton gives our body its shape.

blocks.question: Which of these is an INTERNAL organ (inside the body)?
blocks.explanation: The brain is safely hidden inside your skull. The nose and hands are external.

blocks.question: What is the job of the Heart?
blocks.explanation: The heart pumps blood. The lungs help us breathe, and the brain helps us think!
